Context/Background:
Tumor-infiltrating B cells play a significant role in tumor development, progression, and prognosis, yet a comprehensive classification system is lacking. To address this gap, we present a pan-cancer single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas of tumor-infiltrating B and plasma cells across a large sample cohort. 

We isolated B cells and plasma cells from 15 studies spanning 7 cancer types as data sources. After applying batch correction and integrating the data, we removed low-quality cells and determined the optimal number of clusters. Using standard Seurat methods for integration, clustering, and differential expression analysis, we confirmed the absence of batch effects, with no study- or cancer type-specific clusters. 

We employed a graph-based clustering method to identify TIL-Bs with recurring phenotypes, uncovering a total of 10 clusters. Step one of cluster annotation used canonical markers like CD19 and MS4A1 (CD20), which are prevalent throughout B cell development but decline in plasma cells. Markers such as CD38, JCHAIN, and SDC1 (CD138) are prominent in plasma cells, but less so in earlier stages. This revealed four B cell clusters, two intermediate clusters and four plasma cell clusters.
Prompt: Based on upregulated pathways and differentially expressed markers in each cluster, assign functional phenotypes to each of the 4 Plasma cell clusters (clusters 7-10).  Provide a discussion of the reasoning behind cluster assignments, highlighting important genes and pathways where relevant.

Introduction/Context  
This study integrated tumor-infiltrating B and plasma cells from 15 scRNA-seq cohorts (7 cancer types) using Seurat, removed batch effects, and identified 10 phenotypic clusters. Clusters 7–10 are mature plasma cell populations defined by canonical markers (CD38, JCHAIN, SDC1) with distinct transcriptional programs. Here, we assign functional phenotypes to each plasma cell cluster based on their top differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and enriched pathways.

Keywords  
• Secretory pathway   • Unfolded protein/ER stress   • Heat‐shock response  
• Immunoglobulin isotypes   • Metallothioneins  

Candidate Genes  
• Cluster 7: MZB1, DERL3, SSR4  
• Cluster 8: HSPA6, HSPA1A/B, DNAJB1  
• Cluster 9: IGHA2, IGKC, JCHAIN  
• Cluster 10: MT2A, MT1X, S100A11  

Cluster 7 “ER-High Secretory Plasma Cells”  
• Top DEGs: MZB1, DERL3, FKBP11, SSR4, HSP90B1, numerous Ig light chains (IGKV, IGLC) (avg_log2FC ≈ 2.5–3.2).  
• GSEA (KEGG_2016) shows strong positive NES for “Protein processing in endoplasmic reticulum” (NES ≈ 5.89, FDR < 10⁻⁶) and “Protein export” (NES ≈ 3.10), and negative NES for translation/ribosome terms, reflecting expansion of secretory machinery over general protein synthesis.  
• Function: Highly active antibody‐secreting cells with expanded ER and post-translational folding capacity, specialized for large‐scale immunoglobulin production.  

Cluster 8 “Stress-Response/Chaperone-High Plasma Cells”  
• Top DEGs: HSPA6 (avg_log2FC ≈ 6.65), HSPA1A/B, DNAJB1, HSPB1, JUN, FOS (avg_log2FC ≈ 2.0–4.0).  
• GSEA (Reactome_Pathways_2024) enriched for “Cellular response to heat stress” (NES ≈ 2.25, FDR ≈ 0.10) and “HSF1‐dependent transactivation” (NES ≈ 2.20), and MSigDB_Hallmark “Unfolded Protein Response” trending positive.  
• Function: Plasma cells under proteotoxic/oxidative stress—upregulate chaperones and immediate‐early factors (FOS/JUN) to maintain protein homeostasis during high secretory load or microenvironmental insults.  

Cluster 9 “Classical Ig-Secreting Plasma Cells”  
• Top DEGs: IGHA2, IGKC, IGHG4/2/3, JCHAIN (avg_log2FC ≈ 0.9–1.9), TNFRSF17 (BCMA).  
• While GSEA was sparse at strict FDR, marker composition and high pct.1 expression (e.g., IGKC 0.89 vs. 0.66) indicate strong immunoglobulin and JCHAIN expression.  
• Function: Fully differentiated antibody‐secreting plasma cells producing diverse isotypes (IgA2, IgG subclasses), likely the main effector population in situ.  

Cluster 10 “Metallothionein-Rich/Redox-Regulating Plasma Cells”  
• Top DEGs: MT2A, MT1X, MT1E/F (avg_log2FC ≈ 2.1–4.6), S100A11, GADD45A.  
• ORA (default gene sets) highlights “Metal ion homeostasis” and “Response to zinc/cadmium” (FDR < 0.05), plus “Oxidative stress response” pathways.  
• Function: Metallothionein‐expressing plasma cells specialized in metal sequestration and redox buffering—potentially adapted to hostile tumor microenvironments with high reactive oxygen species or metal fluctuations.  

Discussion  
Together, these four plasma cell clusters span a spectrum from classical high-output secretors (Cluster 7) through stress-adaptive chaperone-high cells (Cluster 8), canonical antibody producers (Cluster 9), to specialized metal-buffering phenotypes (Cluster 10). Cluster 7’s ER-focused program vs. Cluster 8’s heat‐shock signature highlight a division between constitutive secretory capacity and acute stress adaptation. Cluster 9 exemplifies terminal differentiation with broad isotype secretion, while Cluster 10 may represent a protective subset against oxidative or metal‐induced damage. This classification provides a framework for linking plasma cell states to tumor immunity, microenvironmental stress adaptations, and therapy responsiveness.
